mcqs.question: A metal rod of length 2 m has a cross‑sectional area of 5 × 10⁻⁴ m². A tensile force of 500 N is applied along its length. A student incorrectly divides the force by the length to find the stress. What is the correct stress in the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit area: σ = F/A. Here σ = 500 N / (5 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 1 × 10⁶ N/m² = 1 MPa. Dividing by length would give an incorrect quantity (force per length), not stress.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates longitudinal (normal) stress in a solid?

options.A: A cylindrical rod being pulled at both ends
options.B: A block being twisted about its axis
options.C: A beam subjected to a bending moment
options.D: A fluid exerting pressure on the walls of a container

mcqs.answer: A cylindrical rod being pulled at both ends
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal stress occurs when forces act parallel to the cross‑sectional area, producing tension or compression along the length of the material. Pulling a rod at its ends creates exactly this condition. The other options involve shear, bending, or hydrostatic pressure, not longitudinal stress.

mcqs.question: Consider two solids subjected to forces: (i) a cube placed under uniform pressure from all sides, and (ii) a steel bar pulled at its ends. Which statement correctly compares the stresses in the two cases?

options.A: Both experience the same type of stress called bulk stress.
options.B: Case (i) experiences bulk (hydrostatic) stress, while case (ii) experiences longitudinal stress.
options.C: Case (i) experiences shear stress, whereas case (ii) experiences bulk stress.
options.D: Both cases experience only tangential stress.

mcqs.answer: Case (i) experiences bulk (hydrostatic) stress, while case (ii) experiences longitudinal stress.
mcqs.explanation: Uniform pressure acting equally in all directions produces bulk or hydrostatic stress, which is isotropic. Pulling a bar creates normal stress along its length, i.e., longitudinal stress. The other options mix up the nature of the stresses.

mcqs.question: A rectangular block has a top surface area of 0.02 m². A horizontal force of 400 N is applied uniformly over this surface, producing a tangential (shear) stress. What is the magnitude of this stress?
mcqs.explanation: Tangential (shear) stress τ = Force / Area. τ = 400 N / 0.02 m² = 20 000 N/m² = 20 kPa. The other options correspond to incorrect divisions of the force or area.

mcqs.question: In the context of solid mechanics, how is stress defined?

options.A: Force per unit area acting internally within a material
options.B: Force per unit volume acting externally

mcqs.answer: Force per unit area acting internally within a material
mcqs.explanation: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit area that develops inside a material when external forces are applied. It is not related to volume, displacement, or energy per mass.

mcqs.question: If a force of 250 N is applied uniformly on a cross‑sectional area of 5 × 10⁻³ m² of a metal bar, what is the stress in the bar?
mcqs.explanation: Stress σ = F/A = 250 N / (5 × 10⁻³ m²) = 5 × 10⁴ N/m². The other options arise from arithmetic errors such as misplaced decimal points.

mcqs.question: Longitudinal stress in a solid is best described as:

options.A: Stress acting parallel to the cross‑sectional area due to tensile or compressive forces
options.B: Stress acting parallel to the surface causing layers to slide over each other
options.C: Stress resulting from uniform pressure applied from all directions

mcqs.answer: Stress acting parallel to the cross‑sectional area due to tensile or compressive forces
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal (or normal) stress is produced when forces are applied along the length of a material, either pulling (tension) or pushing (compression). Option B describes shear stress, C describes bulk stress, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: A cube of side 0.1 m is placed in a fluid that exerts a uniform pressure of 2 × 10⁵ Pa on all its faces. What is the bulk (hydrostatic) stress experienced by the cube?
mcqs.explanation: Bulk or hydrostatic stress is equal to the external pressure applied uniformly in all directions. Hence the stress equals the fluid pressure, 2 × 10⁵ Pa. The other values are unrelated to the given pressure.
